newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran plans free trade zone on Turkmenistan border.
newsitem.headline: Iran plans free trade zone on Turkmenistan border.

text.p: Iran is planning a free trade zone on its border with Turkmenistan where the Iranian rail network links with those of the Central Asian states, state-run Tehran radio said on Tuesday.
It said the Supreme Council of the Free Trade-Industry Zones, the highest decision-making body for the areas, agreed to set up the zone in Sarakhs and told a commission to study details of the plan.
Iran in May opened a 300 km (190 mile) railway linking its Gulf ports to Sarakhs in a move Tehran said would revive the ancient "Silk Road" and make the country a regional trade hub.
A number of infrastructure projects have been undertaken to develop the region, including an airport, a dam and roads.
Tehran in February 1996 eased its strict foreign exchange rules at border markets in northeastern Khorasan province, where Sarakhs is located, to boost trade.

Iran already has free trade zones in Kish and Qeshm islands and the port of Chah Bahar on the Gulf. They were set up in 1989 to draw foreign investment to reconstruct the economy after the 1980-88 Iran-Iraq war.
